Sentence (English): We had a previous model from the sister brand Neff that was in daily use for 10 years without any problems.
Comments (English): [ Uncomplicated and long-lasting ] || ---------------- || We had a previous model from the sister brand Neff that was in daily use for 10 years without any problems. The new one from Bosch no longer has the usual projector that shows the program and the running time on the floor. There is now a good app for this that informs the user with push notifications on their cell phone when the rinsing process is finished, when the device needs to be cleaned, etc. In the app you can see everything important in real time and you have the option of canceling the rinsing process to start or stop remotely. We are very satisfied with the device.
Comments (Original): [ Unkompliziert und langlebig ] || ---------------- || Wir hatten ein Vorgängermodell der Schwestermarke Neff, das 10 Jahre problemlos im täglichen Gebrauch war. Der neue von Bosch hat nun nicht mehr den gewohnten Projektor, der das Programm und die Laufzeit am Boden anzeigt. Dafür gibt es jetzt eine gute App, die den Nutzer mit Pushmitteilungen auf das Handy darüber informiert, wann der Spülvorgang beendet ist, eine Gerätereinigung erforderlich ist, etc.. In der App bekommt man in Echtzeit alles wichtige angezeigt und man hat die Möglichkeit den Spülvorgang aus der Ferne zu starten oder zu stoppen. Wir sind sehr zufrieden mit dem Gerät.

I would have given 5 stars, but the washing takes soooooo long. I do the quick cycle and it's still OVER AN HOUR. So I think it has more to do with the energy requirements than the washer itself. All in all, one of the best appliance decision we have made in our many years of home ownership. And it even came in white, perhaps out of style but suits our fancy.

Sentence (English): We bought a Bosch dishwasher after having reliability issues with our Kitchenaid, hoping it will last for a long time!
Comments (English): [ Working Great! ] || ---------------- || We bought a Bosch dishwasher after having reliability issues with our Kitchenaid, hoping it will last for a long time! The model has the door open when the cycle ends, which has been great, everything gets nice and dry. The touch pad is a little confusing (you have to hit 3 buttons just to start it) and there is no "rinse only" option. There is a red light that shines on the floor when the cycle starts. One day it was blinking red and wouldn't start. I got on the app to see if it would offer help. It did not. We finally searched google and figured out that the top drawer wasn't all the way back. Looks like the blinking red light just means "something's wrong". The main drawback is that the layout of the racks don't make a lot of sense to me. There are not a lot of rows for glasses on the top rack, and it just doesn't seem as well laid out as the Kitchenaid. There are simple loading illustrations, but I wish they let us know what the designers had in mind with the racks, it is not intuitive to me. The 3rd rack is great. The stainless steel seems to be resisting spots well so far. The main thing is: the dishes are clean!

Sentence (English): We bought two of these units to replace failed units that served us well for over 16 years.
Comments (English): [ No longer cleaning dishes a year in. Disappointing ] || ---------------- || We bought two of these units to replace failed units that served us well for over 16 years. These new ones? One of them failed within a year. The other is surely not long for this world at this rate.Here's what happens: regardless of cycle settings, water only seems to flow from TOP DOWN, never from BOTTOM UP. This means that everything except for cutlery or dishes ends up filthy, with grime baked on, making it only harder to clean by hand. And yes, we made sure the diverter valve and the spray arms are all clean and free from debris. Sometimes it decides to throw another curveball, running water only from the BOTTOM UP, but not from TOP DOWN. There is no rhyme or reason to this, so it's very difficult to predict what kind of dishes are safe to put into this machine.Be careful when you buy - reliability is clearly an issue with this model.

[Reason for Purchase] I was so busy with work and studies that I decided to get a dishwasher. I had heard a lot about how good SK products are, but I missed the timing, and the affordable models on the official website were all sold out. So, I had no choice but to purchase a Samsung product, which was said to be the next best option. [Purchasing Tips] They say that with appliances, bigger is better, but a 12-place setting is too big, and usually, built-in installations look the neatest. Also, since I don't eat at home all the time, I was worried about electricity and water bills. Washing dishes immediately felt wasteful because the amount was small, and I didn't want to collect them to wash later because it would make everything too messy. Above all, there are so many built-in products that it feels like a popular choice when buying a new house. Furthermore, I thought it would be very uncomfortable to have to bend over to use it. That is why I ended up buying this product. However, after using it, I am extremely satisfied! First of all, the technician was very kind and even installed it for me. I called the repair center because I had a question, and a technician came right away. I am extremely satisfied with the after-sales service as well! [Usage Tip]. They say you need to pre-wash it, but for me, it cleaned up squeaky clean even without pre-washing. I bought it to save myself the trouble, so who needs to pre-wash? However, if there is a lot of food residue, the food collection area might overflow, so I recommend rinsing it roughly with water once in a while before using it! Sentence (English): I recently purchased the Samsung 24\" Top Control Built-In Dishwasher, and unfortunately, my experience has been less than satisfactory.
Comments (English): [ 5th service call ] || ---------------- || I recently purchased the Samsung 24\" Top Control Built-In Dishwasher, and unfortunately, my experience has been less than satisfactory. Within just nine months of ownership, I've had to schedule service calls not once, not twice, but four times already, and I'm currently awaiting my fifth. The repeated issues I've encountered are deeply concerning. The laundry list of failures includes the pump, heater, and circuit board, all of which have malfunctioned at various points. This ongoing saga has not only been inconvenient but also a significant disappointment given the initial expectations I had for a reputable brand like Samsung. While the dishwasher's design and features may seem appealing, the constant need for service and the unreliability of its core components have left me frustrated and dissatisfied. I strongly advise potential buyers to consider investing a little more in a higher-quality unit from a different brand. In the long run, it may save you the headache of frequent breakdowns and the inconvenience of multiple service calls. In conclusion, my experience with the Samsung dishwasher has been far from ideal, and I cannot recommend this particular model based on its performance and reliability issues.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher has it all.
Comments (English): [ Quiet and high performance dishwasher ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher has it all. Sleek design, 3 racks for maximum cleaning, and settings galore. The thing I noticed immediately was how quiet it was! You can barely hear it running, which is important for me because our living room and kitchen are close and I'd rather not have to tune out the dishwasher to hear my favorite show. I also love the sleek design. The outside is fingerprint resistant stainless steel, and the interior is a stainless steel tub with dark gray racks. I love that the dark gray racks will show less staining in the years to come. When it comes to features, this thing has it all. First off, it has three racks with the top rack being for larger utensils and smaller things that may fall through the other racks. The middle rack, which would typically be your top rack, has a vast array of space. It has a deep well on the left for large items. There are also bottle jets and clips to help keep your larger bottles upright and get cleaned when the normal sprayer may not reach it entirely. The bottom rack boasts a wide range of arranging. The racks can fold down to accommodate larger cookware as well as removable utensil basket to maximize the bottom rack space. I'm very impressed with the cycles and how effective they are in cleaning our dishes. I have been typically using the auto cycle with a normal dry, but I will be adventuring on to the others soon. I also love that the time remaining is featured on the control panel. Guessing is gone now! GE has definitely outdone themselves with this line and this dishwasher. My two complaints would be that there was no directions on where to put the black trim that came with the dishwasher, and I ultimately figured it out after we had installed it into our cabinet. So I will have to take it out to install the black trim on the sides and top. Our dishwasher is also missing a wheel on the middle rack. We have overcome this by moving one around but ultimately would like a complete unit. Other than that, the installation was straightforward. I was happy that a steel braided hose and drain hose was included. I would love to see more products from the GE Café series as this one is so stylish and upscale.

Comments (English): [ Please, those who are feeding baby food ] || ---------------- || Even when the dishwasher boom was at its peak, I held out, thinking I would get a built-in one once I finally had a house. Now, my baby is six months old. Since my baby started solid foods a bit early, I’ve been making them myself. When we were only breastfeeding, washing bottles was such a hassle, but I had no choice. I did it reluctantly, washing and sterilizing them with boiling water. However, cleaning those baby food cubes was just *so* stressful. I decided I couldn't take it anymore, so I looked into dishwashers. They were much cheaper than I expected! What an idiot I am. Why did I only look into this now? My lazy mind and body have suffered for the past six months. Since all our wedding gifts were LG, I hesitated a bit, but the price was reasonable, and the white color and clean design looked great, so I decided to bring a Samsung into my home! Since it’s a rented apartment, I purchased a countertop model. Ideally, I’d love to get a 12-place setting built-in one, but a homeless person just cries. The countertop models turned out to be quite neat and stylish, too! I bought the 6-person dishwasher because we are a family of three! It is a bit small, but I run it once a day! When making baby food cubes, I run it about twice a day. Putting everything else aside, I am extremely satisfied that I don't have to wash each cube individually. If you are making baby food, please, please, please include a dishwasher in your baby food supplies! All the installation technicians were kind, and they called the day before to schedule the time regarding pre-drilled holes. Since our house already had a pre-drilled hole, they connected it through that hole! I am not 100% satisfied, but 500%. You absolutely must buy this!

The rack wheels (particularly the lowest rack), don't roll as smoothly as previous (GE Profile) machine, and feel a little 'cheap', although functionally they're fine and appear sturdy. I got a good deal on this machine (contractor return) and not sure I need/would pay for the wi-fi. But if quiet is important to you, it's worth its (list) price!

Comments (English): [ I am so in love with my dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Can I just tell you, I never thought I'd say the words "I'm so in love with my dishwasher". but I seriously do it every night when I load it. I LOVE the 3rd rack on top to put long cooking utensils, lids, large knives, etc. I LOVE the fact that I can adjust one or both sides of the middle rack depending on how tall things are on either the bottom or middle rack. I LOVE how everything fits in the dishwasher now and gets so clean! I LOVE how it pops open after the cycle automatically so that things are dry by morning when I unload it. I LOVE that it has a sensor to makes sure it doesn't leak (I had a friend whose kitchen had to be all torn out because her dishwasher leaked - which is one reason why I got this particular dishwasher.) I was skeptical about the price at first - because lets be honest: it's a dishwasher. There are other things I'd rather spend my money on. But I haven't regretted it for one second. I absolutely love it! I was also a little skeptical that it only came with one removable silverware rack that fits on the bottom. I thought for sure all our silverware wouldn't fit - we have 5 in our family. But I've been surprised to find that as long as I use the cover that separates the individual cutlery, I've never had a problem fitting all of them and sometimes it's only half full! And it runs super quiet. There are only 2 drawbacks in my opinion with this dishwasher: 1) Even though this dishwasher itself is quiet, when it drains - the drain is so powerful that the sound from the sink drain is pretty loud. Overall, the pros far outweight the cons. I couldn't be happier - and this coming from a serious tightwad! It's so worth it. You won't regret this purchase!

Sentence (English): While I've only had this dishwasher for a month, and thus cannot comment on it's longevity, I can say that it is as good as all of the rave reviews out there.
Comments (English): [ Great appliance so far ] || ---------------- || While I've only had this dishwasher for a month, and thus cannot comment on it's longevity, I can say that it is as good as all of the rave reviews out there. It's quiet and gets everything squeaky clean. And in spite of some comments I've read, dishes come out dry as a bone. Even the plastic is almost completely dry. It seems that the door automatically popping open at the end of the cycle is not gimmicky - it does help evaporation.Stacking everything does take some getting used to, but that would be true for any new dishwasher. The wife and I love the silverware rack at the top. It's a great design and keeps everything seperated during washing.We love the looks of the exterior - it's a great looking addition to our appliances. And the controls being on the top of the door, hidden from view, not only add to the aesthetics but keep you from turning things on when you bump into the door.I didn't think I'd appreciate the connectivity/app but it turns out that I do. Mostly because it shows how long before the cycle is done. That part is pretty cool.Pretty happy camper here. Let's hope it lasts!

Sentence (English): Purchased Thanksgiving 2023 and we are amazed at how clean and shiny the dishes and glasses come out.
Comments (English): [ The trade offs are totally worth it! ] || ---------------- || Purchased Thanksgiving 2023 and we are amazed at how clean and shiny the dishes and glasses come out. We run our dishwasher almost every day and sometimes twice in one day due to daily cooking at home.I chose this model because it is almost silent. Our previous KitchenAid lasted 8 plus years getting heavy use during covid. I did give up a few features with this model in exchange for the lowest decibel level. It does not have the "top rack only" nor does it tell the cycle time on the lighted top panel but I was willing to give those up for the almost silent sound. Our previous KitchenAid lasted 8 plus years getting heavy use during covid. I did give up a few features with this model in exchange for the lowest decibel level. It does not have the 'top rack only' nor does it tell the cycle time on the lighted top panel but I was willing to give those up for the almost silent sound. I find use of the third level silverware rack a great idea. I never thought I would like it but I took out the bottom silverware rack and fit in more serving bowls, mixing bowls and pots. With the top silverware 'grid' we don't have to bend over repeatedly; we don't worry about knives that little ones might get and the dog no longer runs to lick the spoons and forks! I place each type of silverware in a separate section ( teaspoons together, salad forks together etc) and then emptying silver and placing it in the silverware drawer is SO much faster! In the quest for efficiency and peace I really like the design features and quietness. ( my degree is in home economics) A great purchase reasonably priced.

Comments (English): [ Pricey, but Darn Good ] || ---------------- || We decided on this dishwasher primarily because of its claimed drying capability. The cleaning is very good too. There have been a couple times where it's struggled, but all-in-all, very good performance. It's rare that I need to quickly run -- or run multiple loads, so I generally just leave it on heavy, so cannot comment on the efficacy of lower time cycles. With heavy option and sanitize (which further helps drying), my cycle is just under 3 hrs. I am only giving this 4 stars because it is quite expensive. Compared to a lot of other units in the market, it's a lot. For the price point, my wife and I both thought the drawer slides should have been higher quality. They are not ball-bearing and feel cheap.

Sentence (English): We purchased the Bosch 800 series dishwasher in January 2024.
Comments (English): [ Love our new dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || We purchased the Bosch 800 series dishwasher in January 2024. Our previous dishwasher was a Bosch 500 series that we purchased in 2009 (lasted us close to 15 years) that we replaced only because the front pull-handle panel was cracking and making it very hard to open without further cracking the panel. Our new dishwasher is just as quiet (perhaps more quiet? ) than our previous dishwasher, and we love the sanitize feature. I wasn't a fan of the app-based controls at first, but then I realized I could add the dishwasher to my Alexa routines, and have it run the desired program every night while we're sleeping without ever having to press a single button (just have to remember to add dishwasher soap every evening). The quality of the build is top-notch as you'd expect from a Bosch product. And we love the towel bar, makes it so nice to have a towel nearby for any extra water on large pieces (which is super rare)! Looking forward to another 15 years (fingers crossed) of clean dishes from the new dishwasher!

Sentence (English): For the price, and the Bosch reputation, I'm disappointed.
Comments (English): [ quiet, but with cheap buttons and poor service ] || ---------------- || For the price, and the Bosch reputation, I'm disappointed. It is quiet, as advertised. Doesn't do a great job of drying, but that's not a dealbreaker. What's really bad is that the start button broke -- it became stuck in a down position, and required taking the door apart to fix it. The repair guy showed me how the start button is cheaply made with almost nothing holding it in place, and you have to be careful to press it very gently to prevent getting it stuck. A slightly more robust mechanism to secure the button in place would have prevented this weakness. I didn't think I'd pressed it that hard, and an expensive dishwasher like this shouldn't have such a problem. When I called Bosch for support it was a 45 minute wait, and when I scheduled a repair with them it was a 3 week wait (less than 1 week for the local repair guy I went with instead).

Sentence (English): Purchased Thanksgiving 2023 and we are amazed at how clean and shiny the dishes and glasses come out.
Comments (English): [ The trade offs are totally worth it! ] || ---------------- || Purchased Thanksgiving 2023 and we are amazed at how clean and shiny the dishes and glasses come out. We run our dishwasher almost every day and sometimes twice in one day due to daily cooking at home.I chose this model because it is almost silent. Our previous KitchenAid lasted 8 plus years getting heavy use during covid. I did give up a few features with this model in exchange for the lowest decibel level. It does not have the “top rack only” nor does it tell the cycle time on the lighted top panel but I was willing to give those up for the almost silent sound. I find use of the third level silverware rack a great idea. I never thought I would like it but I took out the bottom silverware rack and fit in more serving bowls, mixing bowls and pots. With the top silverware “grid” we don't have to bend over repeatedly; we don't worry about knives that little ones might get and the dog no longer runs to lick the spoons and forks! I place each type of silverware in a separate section ( teaspoons together, salad forks together etc) and then emptying silver and placing it in the silverware drawer is SO much faster! In the quest for efficiency and peace I really like the design features and quietness. ( my degree is in home economics) A great purchase reasonably priced.

It still is super quiet, does a good job of getting things clean and looks good, and the third rack is really handy. That said, I really wish we had had a third rack Bosch option that did not have an app. We won't ever connect it or any other smart appliance to our WiFi for security and privacy reasons. It does still work, but there are features that are really cumbersome to use without it, like changing the weirdly long "cycle ended" jingle. If it has to be device connected, which I don't really understand in the first place, a Bluetooth only local connection would be better.

Sentence (English): So far so good with this dishwasher, we've had it for 1 month.
Comments (English): [ An upgrade from previous Whirlpool dishwasher ] || ---------------- || So far so good with this dishwasher, we've had it for 1 month. We had what I think was the model 'below' the one we just purchased and the previous one lasted for nearly 9 years before the controller board apparently went out (all lights were on but the dishwasher wouldn't turn on). What I like better about this dishwasher is that it dries much better than our previous Whirlpool model, and while the door on this new one is really stiff, the door doesn't flop open like our previous dishwasher door did if it's not closed tight (dangerous for small kids and pets). The top rack for smaller items is nice but the second rack is then a little lower (just need to get used to this), and while the silverware holder is no longer in the door which I didn't care for previously, it's along the far side of the lower rack and you can only reach a few of the compartments to load silverware without pulling the stiff door all the way open and the bottom rack all the way out to load silverware. I wish I could move the silverware rack to the front of the bottom rack so I could easily reach all of the compartments. The interior is stainless steel while our previous model had a plastic interior (I didn't notice stains or odors in our previous model though), and the exterior is fingerprint resistant which helps to keep it looking cleaner longer. I like that there's a one- or three-hour setting for cleaning and the detergent dispenser seems smaller (less detergent needed) and the dishwasher still cleans the dishes well, and it seems quieter than the previous model we stiff. I really like this dishwasher and hopefully we'll get 10+ years out of this one. I think the door will become less stiff over time with use so my only really complaint is the position of the silverware compartment. Overall, I recommend Whirlpool dishwashers (that's why we purchased a second one) but do your homework on the models before you purchase.

Highly recommend my Bosch dishwasher!

Sentence (English): We purchased this dishwasher directly from Lowe's.
Comments (English): [ Super Quiet ] || ---------------- || We purchased this dishwasher directly from Lowe's. When we hooked it up, it was throwing an error code. I spent loads of time googling the solution and then sat on hold with Bosch Customer support for quite a while. The dishwasher ended up leaking from 2 separate places. Bosch Customer Support gave us the name of a company that could come repair it, but they were more than 3 weeks out. We had already been without a dishwasher for some time, and to have our brand new $1k dishwasher not functioning was quite frustrating. We ended up purchasing the part and fabbing up some cork to seal up both leaks and it functions as intended. I would give it a better rating were it not for our rough start. The dishwasher is extremely quiet, and the third rack for silverware is an excellent feature. Auto Air is nice as well. The only gripe I have about the operation is that none of the lights on top stay on when it is running. It seems that you have to open the door to see what cycle it is on, unless you use the "Home Connect" app to run it remotely.

Sentence (English): We bought our dishwasher from Home Depot and it didn't work.
Comments (English): [ Bit of a 'rocky' start but now all is good ] || ---------------- || We bought our dishwasher from Home Depot and it didn't work. Turns out it wasn't properly installed - the water lines were crimped so nothing worked. During the process to figure out what was wrong I called Bosch twice and each time the phone was promptly answered. The Bosch person spoke English clearly and was easy to understand. She walked me through 'stuff' to see what was wrong and one thought was that no water was getting in to the machine which did turn out to be the problem. I finally figured out not to hit the light but touch the words to select my options. Also 'reset' means on/off. Not sure why they don't just label it as such? It was easy to get connected with a Bosch appliance rep who came out and fixed the water lines. Home Depot did arrange for that and paid for the service visit as they should. I'd like to have the option to choose a short wash. There is the option for a 60 minute cycle but I often used the 30 minute option on my previous dishwasher. Hence the 4 rating.

Sentence (English): The diswasher didn't come with a five-dollar elbow which is essential to installation.
Comments (English): The diswasher didn't come with a five-dollar elbow which is essential to installation. First dishwasher I have ever had that didn't include all the parts. It's a thirty minute one-way trip to Home Depot for me. Added two hours to the installation process. Spent nearly $700 on the unit and they couldn't include a $5 part. Paid $29 for delivery because Home Depot wouldn't accommodate an in store pickup. But, I had to go back to get the part which made the delivery charge a waist of money. Also the unit doesn't work unless you download the Bosch app and agree to let them track your personal data. Unnecessarily complicated. Now to get it to work you must have a functioning internet connection, router and cell phone and let them track you. None of this was mentioned when making the buy decision. Went on vacation for a week and got a message from Bosch saying I haven't used my dishwasher in a while. I don't need that. Low expectations this unit will last very long given the complicated electronics. It has cleaned OK using the auto feature but the drying is not so good. Also, compared to the Whirlpool dishwasher I had before it hold less dishes. I do not recommend this product.

Sentence (English): I recently purchased the Bosch Series 4 Dishwasher, and overall, it has been a satisfactory addition to my kitchen.
Comments (English): [ My Lovely Bosch Series 4 Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I recently purchased the Bosch Series 4 Dishwasher, and overall, it has been a satisfactory addition to my kitchen. Here's a breakdown of what I liked and disliked about this appliance. Things I Liked: Flex Basket System: The Flex Basket System is a game-changer. It creates more space for dishes, allowing me to fit more items in a single load. This means fewer cycles and more efficient cleaning. EcoSilence Drive: The dishwasher operates extremely quietly, which is a huge plus. Its efficient EcoSilence Drive not only keeps noise levels low but also ensures energy efficiency, making it an eco-friendly choice. Efficiency: I've been impressed with the efficiency of the Bosch Series 4 Dishwasher. Even with the Quick option (one-hour cycle), the dishes come out sparkling clean every time. It saves time and water without compromising on performance. WiFi Connectivity: While I didn't find the WiFi connectivity particularly useful, it's a nice feature to have. However, it could be improved to offer more practical functionalities. Things I Didn't Like: Price: The price point of around AUD 1000 seems a bit steep compared to similar dishwashers in its class. While it delivers on its promises, the cost might deter some potential buyers. Product Manual: The instruction manual provided with the dishwasher wasn't as helpful as I had hoped. It lacked clarity and detail, making it difficult to troubleshoot issues or understand all the features. Product Labeling: The model details and serial number on the dishwasher door were poorly labeled. The light gray color and German language made it challenging to read and register the product. Overall, despite some drawbacks, the Bosch Series 4 Dishwasher performs well and meets my expectations. Its efficiency, quiet operation, and practical features make it a worthy investment for those willing to overlook the higher price tag. However, improvements in the product manual and labeling would enhance the overall user experience. Despite its flaws, I would still recommend the Bosch Series 4 Dishwasher to others seeking a reliable and efficient dishwasher for their home.

Sentence (English): My husband and I bought this dishwasher to replace the one that came with our house.
Comments (English): [ Great product + smooth delivery, install, haulaway ] || ---------------- || My husband and I bought this dishwasher to replace the one that came with our house. Our original was a GE and lasted about 5 years (brand new dishwasher that came with our new house). We were looking for a quiet, dependable, long lasting dishwasher that does a great job. After researching on forums, youtube videos, and asking family/friends, we landed on the Bosch 300 Series. We have had our dishwasher for about a little over a month or two, and we love it. Pros: Dishwasher 1.) First, it is very quiet -- our kitchen opens up to the great room and a quiet dishwasher was something we really wanted to reduce extra noise levels (we have 1 dog, 1 toddler, and 1 baby. along with 3 cats. so it can get very loud without the help of a dishwasher). 2.) Second, it cleans our dishes very well -- we run the dishwasher perhaps every 1.5 weeks so sometimes food can dry on the dishes; but this dishwasher has cleaned all the dishes well including baby bottles. I also really like the third rack -- we use it for utensils (which opens up the bottom rack for more dishes, pots/pans, etc. 3.) Third, it looks aesthetically pleasing -- the face of the dishwasher is easy to clean as well. Pros: Ordering through Costco, deliver, install, and haul away 1. Easy. I read about bad experiences so I was hesitant, but glad I went through with it. After ordering, you receive an email that states the third party company that will do install will contact you. I received a text and an email from that company and they were easy to get into contact with. 2. You get a window frame for delivery and a separate one for install (if applicable). For the same day (if you choose this option -- which we did). As the day approached, our delivery time narrowed along with the install time -- we received communication for both. 3. Dishwasher was delivered with no issues. Installer arrived within the time frame, installed our new dishwasher (they had to remove some framing that was present by the builder for our original dishwasher but did not damage any cabinetry, etc; and the new dishwasher looks great like it belongs where it is -- flush with the rest of the surrounding cabinetry). 4. Haulaway -- easy. the installer hauled away the old dishwasher and cleaned up. He brought his own towel to clean up (as it was raining the day of delivery/install/haulaway). Nice guy. Cons: 1. The dishwasher sometimes does not fully dry plastics. However, we open the dishwasher after it finishes it's cycle after at least 30 minutes-1 hr (there's a Bosch dishwasher that automatically does this for you if you pay a bit more), and that seems to do the trick. We highly recommend our dishwasher, the delivery service from Costco, and the install/haul away!

Comments (English): [ We are a family of three with children, and the children eat food and the adults eat food. ] || ---------------- || We are a family of three with children, and as we make food for the children and food for the adults, the amount of dishwashing becomes enormous. It's good to eat the same menu, but that's not always possible, and adults sometimes crave spicy foods. Especially on weekends when the three of us all gathered together to eat, the amount of dishwashing in the morning was no joke, and when I turned around and looked at the sink after eating a meal, I sighed, and my husband also said he would do it himself, but when he saw that amount, he thought, should I just buy a dishwasher? So I ordered it right away. I wanted to receive it sooner, but there was no available date, so I waited a little longer than expected. Installation was very quick and the technicians were very friendly. More than anything, I was most worried about whether it would be possible to install it, but fortunately it was in the right spot and I was able to install it without canceling! I've been using it for over half a year, and I really like it because I don't have to worry about washing dishes while cooking. Sometimes I hated washing dishes so much that I ordered them to eat, but now I'm happy that it's not like that. There are special courses for washing dishes, but I'm worried about that, so I do it myself. I put all the glass, wok, frying pan, and silicone containers in them and turn them all at once! When the time comes, it will tell you to clean the inside, and when you turn it on, the door will open on its own to dry out all the water. I really regret why I didn't buy it sooner, and I don't even want to think about going back to the way it was before I bought it. +) Even though we are a family of 3, we were forced(?) to buy a 14-person unit in order to match the size of the under-sink cabinet. (No matter how much I thought about the size that could be installed in the space where it was currently installed, I couldn't figure it out.) As expected, home appliances are called Geogeoikseon. I guess that makes sense. I usually do it once a day, after dinner. My child goes to daycare and eats a morning snack and lunch, so in the morning, he just eats milk, fruit, and bread, so there is no need to do the dishes. So, when I stay at home, I eat breakfast once and then cook dinner and eat that meal once, but even though I don't eat anything big, my insides are full. It seems the bigger the better.

Sentence (English): I purchased this dishwasher to replace an LG Quadwash unit that basically fell apart after 5 years.
Comments (English): [ Fine, as long as you don't pay full price. ] || ---------------- || I purchased this dishwasher to replace an LG Quadwash unit that basically fell apart after 5 years.This is Bosch's entry level machine and as such it doesn't have all the bells and whistles of the models further up in the range.Installation was straightforward and problem-free, but note that the Aqua Stop device is a bit bigger than on some other brands, so you might need to make the feed-through hole in your kitchen cabinet a bit bigger (I did). Bosch says you need an 80mm diameter hole, so worth remembering that.What I like: Very simple and super easy to use (this was important to me), with just one knob to select from the four cycles available. And I like the fact there are only four cycles and one option to choose from - I found that on our last machine we almost exclusively used the same cycle. We just didn't need or use all the extra cycles and options available.The washing result is excellent - everything comes out squeaky clean in a reasonable amount of time.Things not so good (but not that important to me): No fold down tines in the lower rack. It's a bit thirsty (it can use up to 19 litres on the Auto cycle). It is quite stinky inside at first, but the smell dissipates after several uses. No end of cycle indication. After the cycle finishes the timer displays 0.00 but switches off after 1 minute. This can however be changed in Settings so that 0.00 will stay on indefinitely, indicating that the cycle has finished. Note there is no audible chime or tune when the cycles finishes. The shiny stainless steel finish on the door doesn't really match the control panel or plinth very well. There is no "easy lift" top basket, although you can change the height by removing the top basket and choosing from one of the two heights available. I find I always leave it on the higher setting anyway, so doesn't really matter.Annoyances: The control panel is curved so it cannot match your kitchen cupboards for a nice clean installed look. The drying performance out of the box is a bit average. You can enable Intensive Drying in settings - I haven't tried that yet though. The general build quality feels like it has been built down to a price. The racks don't glide very smoothly, the control knob and button actions are decidedly flimsy and cheap feeling. Whether this will mean anything towards long term reliability I don't know, but it certainly makes the day to day use slightly less satisfying.Finally be aware that this dishwasher is pretty noisy (Bosch quotes 50db, which is on par with most similarly priced competitors). For me this doesn't really matter as I only ever run it during the day (to take advantage of solar power). However if you do like to run it overnight when the house is quiet it's worth noting, and you might need to spend a bit more to get something quieter.At full retail of $999 I doubt I would recommend this machine. There are better options available for the price.However I paid $669 at The Good Guys, and at this price I am very happy with what I got for the money.

As a single household, I only do the dishes every other day, so I didn't feel the need for a dishwasher. However, while cooking at home recently, I realized what a "dishwashing hell" truly is. I decided I needed to buy one immediately. I naturally thought I should get the 12-place setting, but besides installation issues, I would have to bend my back every day—and I suffer from back pain. Since it is generally recommended not to use coated pots and pans anyway, I figured this capacity would be sufficient. I considered the Objet Collection because the design was prettier, but I passed on it because although it features hot air drying, it doesn't dry perfectly, and it lacks a door-opening function after washing. I was so satisfied with my previous dish dryer that I wanted to buy the latest model with hot air drying, but the staff member told me that even that doesn't dry perfectly, so I passed on that as well. So, there was only one conclusion: the Samsung Bespoke Desktop 6-place setting! Natural marble non-drilling installation. I thought the Samsung installation team would drill into the natural marble for an extra fee, but that wasn't the case. You need to have the holes drilled in advance to install it. But for a 400,000 won dishwasher, isn't it a bit unreasonable to pay over 100,000 won for the drilling? (Though if I had lived in this house for over 3 years, I probably would have drilled them anyway). So, I racked my brain trying to figure out a way to install it without drilling into the marble, and I installed it as shown in the picture. Since I drilled into the sink cabinet door, I didn't spend any money on it. The white line is a bit bothersome, but it's not bad :). Product performance and satisfaction: The noise is a bit loud for a while after starting, but it's not loud enough to require moving away, so you can still watch TV. After the automatic opening following a wash cycle, quite a bit of water condenses, but if you leave it as is, it will automatically dry. As the water dries on the wine glasses, some stains appear as shown in the picture. I use a lot of large 27cm plates; they lie flat when placed inside, which is fine, but it is a bit inconvenient when putting them in and taking them out. Since there is space left at the top after putting the dishes in, I tried placing a cutting board or frying pan on it and running it, but the washing blades at the top were covered, so the dishes didn't get cleaned thoroughly. When putting in tall dishes like pots... Please make sure to check that the upper washing blades do not touch the dishes. I used to cut the unscented EcoVerve one in half to use it, but when I ran it with plates or frying pans that smelled of fish, the dishes still had a fishy odor. This issue was completely resolved when I switched to the Mandarin scent. After using it for about a month, I found that the condition of coated pots didn't improve, so I have to hand-wash them, as well as plastic items. Comments (English): [ I had a lot of trouble installing it, but I am satisfied. ] || ---------------- || Reasons for choosing the Samsung 6-place setting dishwasher. As a single household, I only do the dishes every other day, so I didn't feel the need for a dishwasher. However, while cooking at home recently, I realized what a "dishwashing hell" truly is. I decided I needed to buy one immediately. I naturally thought I should get the 12-place setting, but besides installation issues, I would have to bend my back every day—and I suffer from back pain. Since it is generally recommended not to use coated pots and pans anyway, I figured this capacity would be sufficient. I considered the Objet Collection because the design was prettier, but I passed on it because although it features hot air drying, it doesn't dry perfectly, and it lacks a door-opening function after washing. I was so satisfied with my previous dish dryer that I wanted to buy the latest model with hot air drying, but the staff member told me that even that doesn't dry perfectly, so I passed on that as well. So, there was only one conclusion: the Samsung Bespoke Desktop 6-place setting! Natural marble non-drilling installation. I thought the Samsung installation team would drill into the natural marble for an extra fee, but that wasn't the case. You need to have the holes drilled in advance to install it. But for a 400,000 won dishwasher, isn't it a bit unreasonable to pay over 100,000 won for the drilling? (Though if I had lived in this house for over 3 years, I probably would have drilled them anyway). So, I racked my brain trying to figure out a way to install it without drilling into the marble, and I installed it as shown in the picture. Since I drilled into the sink cabinet door, I didn't spend any money on it. The white line is a bit bothersome, but it's not bad :). Product performance and satisfaction: The noise is a bit loud for a while after starting, but it's not loud enough to require moving away, so you can still watch TV. After the automatic opening following a wash cycle, quite a bit of water condenses, but if you leave it as is, it will automatically dry. As the water dries on the wine glasses, some stains appear as shown in the picture. I use a lot of large 27cm plates; they lie flat when placed inside, which is fine, but it is a bit inconvenient when putting them in and taking them out. Since there is space left at the top after putting the dishes in, I tried placing a cutting board or frying pan on it and running it, but the washing blades at the top were covered, so the dishes didn't get cleaned thoroughly. When putting in tall dishes like pots... Please make sure to check that the upper washing blades do not touch the dishes. I used to cut the unscented EcoVerve one in half to use it, but when I ran it with plates or frying pans that smelled of fish, the dishes still had a fishy odor. This issue was completely resolved when I switched to the Mandarin scent. After using it for about a month, I found that the condition of coated pots didn't improve, so I have to hand-wash them, as well as plastic items. It is a bit of a hassle, but aside from that, I am very satisfied. I think I made the right choice buying the 6-person size. Not having to bend over is the best! The capacity is just right too! ### Thank you for reading. If this was helpful, I would appreciate it if you clicked "Helpful" :)

I decided I needed to buy one immediately. I naturally thought I should get the 12-place setting, but besides installation issues, I would have to bend my back every day—and I suffer from back pain. Since it is generally recommended not to use coated pots and pans anyway, I figured this capacity would be sufficient. I considered the Objet Collection because the design was prettier, but I passed on it because although it features hot air drying, it doesn't dry perfectly, and it lacks a door-opening function after washing. I was so satisfied with my previous dish dryer that I wanted to buy the latest model with hot air drying, but the staff member told me that even that doesn't dry perfectly, so I passed on that as well. So, there was only one conclusion: the Samsung Bespoke Desktop 6-place setting! Natural marble non-drilling installation. I thought the Samsung installation team would drill into the natural marble for an extra fee, but that wasn't the case. You need to have the holes drilled in advance to install it. But for a 400,000 won dishwasher, isn't it a bit unreasonable to pay over 100,000 won for the drilling? (Though if I had lived in this house for over 3 years, I probably would have drilled them anyway). So, I racked my brain trying to figure out a way to install it without drilling into the marble, and I installed it as shown in the picture. Since I drilled into the sink cabinet door, I didn't spend any money on it. The white line is a bit bothersome, but it's not bad :). Product performance and satisfaction: The noise is a bit loud for a while after starting, but it's not loud enough to require moving away, so you can still watch TV. After the automatic opening following a wash cycle, quite a bit of water condenses, but if you leave it as is, it will automatically dry. As the water dries on the wine glasses, some stains appear as shown in the picture. I use a lot of large 27cm plates; they lie flat when placed inside, which is fine, but it is a bit inconvenient when putting them in and taking them out. Since there is space left at the top after putting the dishes in, I tried placing a cutting board or frying pan on it and running it, but the washing blades at the top were covered, so the dishes didn't get cleaned thoroughly. When putting in tall dishes like pots... Please make sure to check that the upper washing blades do not touch the dishes. I used to cut the unscented EcoVerve one in half to use it, but when I ran it with plates or frying pans that smelled of fish, the dishes still had a fishy odor. This issue was completely resolved when I switched to the Mandarin scent. After using it for about a month, I found that the condition of coated pots didn't improve, so I have to hand-wash them, as well as plastic items. It is a bit of a hassle, but aside from that, I am very satisfied. I think I made the right choice buying the 6-person size. Not having to bend over is the best! The capacity is just right too! ### Thank you for reading. If this was helpful, I would appreciate it if you clicked "Helpful" :)

Sentence (English): 5 star on the product itself…1 star on the installation instructions/engineering.
Comments (English): [ Great machine. Difficult to install. ] || ---------------- || 5 star on the product itself…1 star on the installation instructions/engineering. The engineers on this team understood the assignment and built a machine that cleans and dries dishes beautifully. I cannot say the same for the folks who designed and engineered the installation or the instruction writers. Let's start with the fact that you must wear gloves when installing or you will absolutely slice your fingers to shreds. Edward scissorhands has nothing on this dishwasher. Wear gloves. Don't take a chance. The cuts are deep and will burn from every lemon and lime you slice when you're making your celebration margarita. Oh the salt will sting too…. for days. Don't celebrate too early either. The instructions for how you connect the water make absolutely zero sense. It took me thirty minutes to find the electrical hookup because the drawings are crap (electrical hookup is on the front of the machine, right site when you are facing the door, near the floor, under the rubber flap in an electrical box that you have to take apart to complete the wiring to a (not included) wiring harness/plug)…you're welcome). Very little text and the drawings are too tiny to read or see/understand. If your drain line goes to the right, you're going to have a heck of a time. Whoever designed this thing never installed a dishwasher into a cabinet. The hose clip meant to hold the hose will not work because the hose will stick out beyond the cabinet opening no matter how hard you try. If your line goes left you'll probably be ok because you can snake the line back as you push the dishwasher back. But if it goes to the right you will need to gorilla tape the hose low where the clip is but to the left about 5” so the hose can bend but will be held as low as the clip. I didn't clip or tape it the first time and when I pulled the dishwasher out after running a few times to level it and make sure there were no leaks, the hose had burn marks on it from being situated near (I'm guessing) a heating component. The hose would have eventually burned through and leaked no doubt at all. I also had to tape the electrical cord up so that it wouldn't drop under the feet when pushing the machine back. Not ideal and very frustrating (at this point you're realizing your fingers are sliced to bits too. You will be frustrated and questioning every decision you've made in life including why you chose this dishwasher) but don't give up you're almost there. Don't forget the cabinet hooks. You will, and when you do you'll remember this review say a few choice words and then pull it out again to get the hooks back on. After this it's downhill if you have it leveled and if you have enough space to get the dishwasher gasket thingys in the tiniest space between your cabinets. Love the concept because I'm sure this reduces sound (and this bad boy is quiet I'll tell you) but there's got to be a better way. I messed up my Formica piece on one side of the cabinet from pushing the dishwasher into and out of the gap so many times. The gasket thingys eventually pulled the Formica off and cracked it so that's something I'll have to fix. I have no solution for you on this problem. If you're cabinets are tight you'll have to push like the dickens but by this time you're so mad you don't care and will kick it in if you have to. Of course you could let a Best Buy installer do this for you but I'm thrifty and like doing things myself. If the dishwasher doesn't sit flush make them install it correctly until it does. Cleans great. Easy to load. The door opens and closes easily. The settings are easy to set (you have to push start again if you open during cycle). The water drains loudly. Not because of the pump but because it pushes the water out so quickly. That's a little annoying I'll be honest. Overall I'm very happy with this machine now that my fingers are healed. Glasses and plastic are clean and dry. Love the third rack and the foldable tines for pots. I use the adjustable middle rack to fit everything, Glasses are held up during wash cycle (don't fall over), wine glasses fit nicely, little plates fit in the middle top rack and all other petty concerns. Generally a 2 hour cycle for heavily spoiled dishes but a 1.5 hour cycle works for light loads. Have fun and enjoy. Don't forget your gloves.
